questions.stem: Which organization administers the Certified Surgical Technologist (CST) credentialing examination?
questions.explanation: The National Board of Surgical Technology and Surgical Assisting (NBSTSA) administers the CST exam.

questions.stem: The legal doctrine 'res ipsa loquitur' means:
questions.explanation: Res ipsa loquitur means the negligence is obvious from the event itself (for example, a retained instrument), so proof of fault is inferred.

questions.stem: Who is ultimately responsible for obtaining the patient's informed consent for a surgical procedure?
questions.explanation: The surgeon explains risks, benefits and alternatives. Others may witness the signature but do not obtain the consent.

questions.stem: Surgical conscience is best described as:
options: A personal commitment to honesty and correct sterile technique, even when no one is watching
A legal requirement to report all sterile technique errors to the state
The surgeon's right to choose the surgical team
The policy for counting sponges and sharps
questions.explanation: Surgical conscience is the internal ethical awareness that drives a team member to admit and correct a break in sterile technique.

questions.stem: A surgical technologist notices a neighbor's name on the operating room schedule and mentions it to a friend. This action violates:
questions.explanation: HIPAA protects the privacy of patient health information. Even confirming that a person is a patient is a breach.

questions.stem: The three basic principles of protection from ionizing radiation are:
questions.explanation: Limit exposure time, increase distance from the source, and use shielding such as lead aprons, thyroid shields and barriers.

questions.stem: In the RACE fire response acronym, the letter 'A' stands for:
questions.explanation: RACE = Rescue, Alarm, Contain, Extinguish/Evacuate.

questions.stem: What is the FIRST step in using a fire extinguisher according to the PASS method?
options: Aim at the base of the fire
questions.explanation: PASS = Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep.

questions.stem: Standard precautions apply to:
options: Only patients known to have bloodborne disease
All patients, regardless of diagnosis or infection status
questions.explanation: Standard precautions treat blood and body fluids of every patient as potentially infectious.

questions.stem: During laser surgery, which personnel must wear wavelength-specific protective eyewear?
options: Only the surgical technologist and surgeon
questions.explanation: All personnel need eyewear matched to the laser wavelength; the patient's eyes are protected with moistened pads or appropriate shields.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most reliable monitor to verify that sterilization conditions were achieved?
options: A visual check of the package
questions.explanation: Biological indicators contain resistant bacterial spores and are the only monitor that confirms microorganisms were killed.

questions.stem: Which area of a sterile surgical gown is considered sterile once the gown is donned?
options: The entire gown including the back and neckline
The front from the neckline to the hem
Only the front of the gown below the waist
The front from the chest to the level of the sterile field, and the sleeves from 2 inches above the elbow to the cuff
questions.explanation: The back, neckline, shoulders, underarms and anything below the level of the sterile field are considered unsterile.

questions.stem: A wrapped sterile package is found to have moisture on the outside after being removed from the sterilizer. The package should be:
options: Used if the moisture dries within 5 minutes
Used because the inside is likely dry
questions.explanation: Moisture can wick microorganisms through the wrap; wet packages are treated as contaminated.

questions.stem: Immediate-use (flash) steam sterilization is acceptable ONLY when:
options: It will save time between cases
The facility wishes to avoid purchasing extra instrument sets
There is not enough time to process an item needed immediately by the preferred method
The item is an implant that is easy to reprocess
questions.explanation: IUSS is for urgent, unplanned situations such as a dropped instrument, never for convenience or routine use.

questions.stem: During a surgical hand scrub, the hands should be held:
options: At the same level as the elbows
questions.explanation: Water must run from the cleanest area (fingertips) toward the elbows and drip off the elbows.

questions.stem: When donning a gown and gloves with the closed-glove technique, the hands must:
options: Be extended out of the cuffs before touching the gloves
Be rinsed with alcohol before glove application
Stay inside the cuffs of the gown sleeves until the gloves are on
Remain at the level of the waist
questions.explanation: The closed technique keeps bare hands from ever touching the outside of the glove cuff or gown sleeve.

questions.stem: Which level of disinfection destroys all microorganisms except large numbers of bacterial spores?
questions.explanation: High-level disinfection is used for semi-critical items; sterilization is required for critical items.

questions.stem: A chemical indicator tape on the outside of a wrapped package shows that:
options: The sterilizer has no air entrapment
The package has been exposed to the sterilization process
All spores in the load were killed
questions.explanation: External tape only differentiates processed from unprocessed packages; it does not prove sterility.

questions.stem: Items sterilized with ethylene oxide must undergo:
options: Aeration to remove toxic gas residue
questions.explanation: EO is toxic and flammable; items require a mechanical aeration period before use.

questions.stem: The sterility of a packaged item is best determined by:
options: Event-related factors such as package integrity and handling
The number of days since sterilization alone
questions.explanation: Event-related shelf life: an item stays sterile until an event (tear, moisture, compression) compromises the package.

questions.stem: Metzenbaum scissors are used to:
questions.explanation: Metzenbaum scissors have long, thin blades for delicate tissue; Mayo scissors are used for heavier tissue and sutures.

questions.stem: Babcock forceps are used to grasp:
options: Delicate tubular structures such as bowel or fallopian tube
questions.explanation: The Babcock has fenestrated, atraumatic tips. Allis clamps grasp tougher tissue such as fascia.

questions.stem: Which instrument is used to hold and drive a curved suture needle?
questions.explanation: The needle holder grips the needle about two-thirds from the point (one-third from the swage).

questions.stem: Which of the following is a self-retaining retractor commonly used in abdominal surgery?
questions.explanation: Self-retaining retractors hold the incision open without a team member; the others listed are handheld.

questions.stem: Kelly, Crile, and mosquito instruments are all examples of:
questions.explanation: Hemostats clamp blood vessels; they differ by size and jaw serrations.

questions.stem: Which of the following suture sizes has the smallest diameter?
questions.explanation: The more zeros, the smaller the diameter. 6-0 is finer than 4-0 and 2-0.

questions.stem: Which of the following suture materials is absorbable?
questions.explanation: Polyglactin 910 is a synthetic absorbable suture. Nylon, steel and polypropylene are nonabsorbable.

questions.stem: A taper-point needle is typically used on:
options: Tissue that is easily penetrated such as intestine or peritoneum
questions.explanation: Taper needles pass through tissue without cutting it; cutting needles are used on tough tissue such as skin.

questions.stem: The dispersive pad (return electrode) used with monopolar electrosurgery should be placed on:
options: A large, well-vascularized muscular area close to the surgical site
questions.explanation: Good contact over a large, clean, dry muscle area prevents burns at the pad site.

questions.stem: Which suction tip has multiple holes and is commonly used in the abdominal cavity?
questions.explanation: The Poole suction tip has a sleeve with several openings to prevent tissue from clogging it; the Yankauer is used in open wounds and the oropharynx.

questions.stem: Which gas is most commonly used to insufflate the abdomen during laparoscopic surgery?
questions.explanation: CO2 is absorbed quickly and does not support combustion, making it the safest choice.

questions.stem: A pneumatic tourniquet is used on an extremity to:
options: Increase blood flow to the limb
questions.explanation: The cuff is inflated to temporarily stop arterial inflow; the time and pressure are documented.

questions.stem: Which items are typically placed on the Mayo stand?
options: All instruments and sutures for the case
The instruments the surgeon uses most frequently at that moment
Only the items that need to be counted
questions.explanation: The Mayo stand holds the immediately needed, frequently used instruments; the back table holds the rest.

questions.stem: Surgical sponges contain a radiopaque marker so that:
options: They can be detected on X-ray if one is retained
They can be reused after washing
questions.explanation: The marker allows a retained sponge to be located radiographically.

questions.stem: Which drain is a closed-suction drain with a bulb reservoir?
questions.explanation: The Jackson-Pratt uses a compressed bulb to create gentle suction; the Penrose is a passive, open drain.

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Which phase of wound healing involves granulation tissue and collagen formation?
questions.explanation: During the proliferative phase fibroblasts lay down collagen, new capillaries form and granulation tissue fills the wound.

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Healing by primary intention describes a wound that:
options: Is left open and heals from the inside out
Is closed several days later after infection clears
Has its edges approximated and heals with minimal scarring
questions.explanation: A clean surgical incision closed with sutures, staples or adhesive heals by primary intention.

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Bone wax is used to control bleeding from:
options: Organ surfaces such as the liver
questions.explanation: Bone wax mechanically seals bleeding from cut bone (for example during sternotomy).

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: Evisceration is best defined as:
options: Protrusion of abdominal organs through a wound opening
Partial separation of the skin edges only
questions.explanation: Dehiscence is separation of wound layers; evisceration is the protrusion of viscera and is a surgical emergency.

questions.section: Hemostasis, Wound Healing, and Wound Closure
questions.stem: A ligature is:
options: A tool used to cut tissue
A strand of suture material used to tie off a vessel
questions.explanation: Ligatures (ties) occlude vessels to stop bleeding; free ties and suture ligatures are both used.

questions.stem: Which is the innermost layer of the abdominal wall?
questions.explanation: From outside in: skin, subcutaneous tissue, fascia and muscle, then parietal peritoneum.

questions.stem: An appendectomy incision is made at McBurney's point, located in the:
questions.explanation: McBurney's point lies about one-third of the way from the anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus on the right.

questions.stem: The gallbladder stores and concentrates:
questions.explanation: Bile is produced in the liver and stored in the gallbladder; the cystic duct joins the common hepatic duct to form the common bile duct.

questions.stem: Which heart valve lies between the left atrium and left ventricle?
questions.explanation: The mitral valve controls flow from the left atrium into the left ventricle.

questions.stem: Which lobe of the cerebrum is primarily responsible for vision?
questions.explanation: The occipital lobe at the back of the brain processes visual information.

questions.stem: What is the largest artery in the body?
questions.explanation: The aorta carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle to the systemic circulation.

questions.stem: How many lobes does the right lung have?
questions.explanation: The right lung has three lobes (upper, middle, lower); the left has two because of the cardiac notch.

questions.stem: Which structure carries urine from the kidney to the bladder?
questions.explanation: The ureters transport urine from each kidney to the bladder; the urethra carries it out of the body.

questions.stem: The anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) is located in the:
questions.explanation: The ACL stabilizes the knee by preventing excessive forward movement of the tibia.

questions.stem: Which gland, located on top of each kidney, secretes epinephrine?
questions.explanation: The adrenal medulla releases epinephrine and norepinephrine in the fight-or-flight response.
